results.transcription: He passes abruptly from persons to ideas and numbers, and from ideas and numbers to persons, from the heavens to man, from astronomy to physiology. results.transcription: In the supposed depths of this dialogue, the Neo-Platonists found hidden meanings in connections with the Jewish and Christian scriptures, and out of them, they elicited doctrines quite at variance with the spirit of Plato.

results.transcription: They were absorbed in his theology and were under the dominion of his name. While that which was truly great and truly characteristic in him, his effort to realize and connect abstractions was not understood by them at all.

results.transcription: The fancies of the Neoplatnists are only interesting to us because they exhibit a phase of the human mind which prevailed widely in the first centuries of the Christian era and is not wholly extinct in our own day.

results.transcription: We do not know how Plato would have arranged his own dialogues, or whether the thought of arranging any of them, besides the two trilogies which he has expressly connected, was ever present to his mind.

results.transcription: The dialogue is primarily concerned with the animal creation, including under this term the heavenly bodies, and with man only as one among the animals.

results.reference_text: BUT HE HAS NOT AS YET DEFINED THIS INTERMEDIATE TERRITORY WHICH LIES SOMEWHERE BETWEEN MEDICINE AND MATHEMATICS AND HE WOULD HAVE FELT THAT THERE WAS AS GREAT AN IMPIETY IN RANKING THEORIES OF PHYSICS FIRST IN THE ORDER OF KNOWLEDGE AS IN PLACING THE BODY BEFORE THE SOUL
results.transcription: But he has not as yet defined this intermediate territory which lies somewhere between medicine and mathematics, and he would have felt that there was as great an impiety in ranking theories of physics first in the order of knowledge as in placing the body before the soul.

results.reference_text: WITH HERACLEITUS HE ACKNOWLEDGES THE PERPETUAL FLUX LIKE ANAXAGORAS HE ASSERTS THE PREDOMINANCE OF MIND ALTHOUGH ADMITTING AN ELEMENT OF NECESSITY WHICH REASON IS INCAPABLE OF SUBDUING LIKE THE PYTHAGOREANS HE SUPPOSES THE MYSTERY OF THE WORLD TO BE CONTAINED IN NUMBER
results.transcription: With Heraclitus, he acknowledges the perpetual flux. Like an exagerus, he asserts the predominance of mind, although admitting an element of necessity which reason is incapable of subduing. Like the Pythagorean, he supposes the mystery of the world to be contained in number.

results.transcription: The style and plan of the Timeas differ greatly from bad of any other of the Platonic dialogues.

results.transcription: And hence, we find the same sort of clumsiness in the Temeas of Plato, which characterizes the philosophical poem of Lucretius.

results.reference_text: THERE IS A WANT OF FLOW AND OFTEN A DEFECT OF RHYTHM THE MEANING IS SOMETIMES OBSCURE AND THERE IS A GREATER USE OF APPOSITION AND MORE OF REPETITION THAN OCCURS IN PLATO'S EARLIER WRITINGS
results.transcription: There is a want of flow, and often a defect of rhythm. The meaning is sometimes obscure, and there is a greater use of opposition and more of repetition than occurs in Plato's earlier writings.

results.transcription: But already at a point in economic evolution far and dating the emergence of the lady, specialized consumption of goods as an evidence of pecuniary strength had begun to work out in a more or less elaborate system.

results.transcription: So, those offices which are by right the proper employment of the leisure class are noble, such as government fighting, hunting the care of arms and accoutrements and the like. In short, those switch may be classed as ostensibly predatory employment.

results.reference_text: IN ORDER TO PLEASE HER I SPOKE TO HER OF THE ABBE CONTI AND I HAD OCCASION TO QUOTE TWO LINES OF THAT PROFOUND WRITER
results.transcription: In order to please her, I spoke to her of the Abby Conti, and I had occasion to quote two lines of that profound writer.

results.reference_text: MADAM CORRECTED ME WITH A PATRONIZING AIR FOR MY PRONUNCIATION OF THE WORD SCEVRA WHICH MEANS DIVIDED SAYING THAT IT OUGHT TO BE PRONOUNCED SCEURA AND SHE ADDED THAT I OUGHT TO BE VERY GLAD TO HAVE LEARNED SO MUCH ON THE FIRST DAY OF MY ARRIVAL IN PARIS TELLING ME THAT IT WOULD BE AN IMPORTANT DAY IN MY LIFE
results.transcription: Madame corrected me with a patronizing heir for my pronunciation of the word scavra, which means divided, saying that it ought to be pronounced skewera. And she added that I ought to be very glad to have learned so much on the first day of my arrival in Paris, telling me that it would be an important day in my life.

results.reference_text: HER FACE WAS AN ENIGMA FOR IT INSPIRED EVERYONE WITH THE WARMEST SYMPATHY AND YET IF YOU EXAMINED IT ATTENTIVELY THERE WAS NOT ONE BEAUTIFUL FEATURE SHE COULD NOT BE CALLED HANDSOME BUT NO ONE COULD HAVE THOUGHT HER UGLY
results.transcription: Her face was an enigma, for it inspired everyone with the warmest sympathy. And yet, if you examined it attentively, there was not one beautiful feature. She could not be called handsome, but no one could have thought her ugly.

results.reference_text: SILVIA WAS THE ADORATION OF FRANCE AND HER TALENT WAS THE REAL SUPPORT OF ALL THE COMEDIES WHICH THE GREATEST AUTHORS WROTE FOR HER ESPECIALLY OF THE PLAYS OF MARIVAUX FOR WITHOUT HER HIS COMEDIES WOULD NEVER HAVE GONE TO POSTERITY
results.transcription: Sylvia was the adoration of France, and her talent was the real support of all the comedies, which the greatest authors wrote for her, especially of the plays of Marivot. For without her, his comedies would never have gone to prosperity.

results.reference_text: SILVIA DID NOT THINK THAT HER GOOD CONDUCT WAS A MERIT FOR SHE KNEW THAT SHE WAS VIRTUOUS ONLY BECAUSE HER SELF LOVE COMPELLED HER TO BE SO AND SHE NEVER EXHIBITED ANY PRIDE OR ASSUMED ANY SUPERIORITY TOWARDS HER THEATRICAL SISTERS ALTHOUGH SATISFIED TO SHINE BY THEIR TALENT OR THEIR BEAUTY THEY CARED LITTLE ABOUT RENDERING THEMSELVES CONSPICUOUS BY THEIR VIRTUE
results.transcription: Sylvia did not think that her good conduct was a merit. For she knew that she was virtuous only because her self-love compelled her to be so, and she never exhibited any pride or assumed any superiority towards her theatrical sisters. Although satisfied to shine by their talent or their beauty, they cared little about rendering themselves conspicuous by their virtue.

results.reference_text: TWO YEARS BEFORE HER DEATH I SAW HER PERFORM THE CHARACTER OF MARIANNE IN THE COMEDY OF MARIVAUX AND IN SPITE OF HER AGE AND DECLINING HEALTH THE ILLUSION WAS COMPLETE
results.transcription: Two years before her death, I saw her perform the character of Marianne in the comedy of Merevo, and in spite of her age and declining health, the illusion was complete.

results.reference_text: SHE WAS HONOURABLY BURIED IN THE CHURCH OF SAINT SAUVEUR WITHOUT THE SLIGHTEST OPPOSITION FROM THE VENERABLE PRIEST WHO FAR FROM SHARING THE ANTI CHRISTAIN INTOLERANCY OF THE CLERGY IN GENERAL SAID THAT HER PROFESSION AS AN ACTRESS HAD NOT HINDERED HER FROM BEING A GOOD CHRISTIAN AND THAT THE EARTH WAS THE COMMON MOTHER OF ALL HUMAN BEINGS AS JESUS CHRIST HAD BEEN THE SAVIOUR OF ALL MANKIND
results.transcription: She was honorably buried in the Church of St. Severe. Without the slightest opposition from the venerable priest who, far from sharing the anti-Christian intolerancy of the clergy in general, said that her profession as an actress had not hindered her from being a good Christian, and that the earth was a common mother of all human beings, as Jesus Christ had been the savior of all mankind.

results.reference_text: YOU WILL FORGIVE ME DEAR READER IF I HAVE MADE YOU ATTEND THE FUNERAL OF SILVIA TEN YEARS BEFORE HER DEATH BELIEVE ME I HAVE NO INTENTION OF PERFORMING A MIRACLE YOU MAY CONSOLE YOURSELF WITH THE IDEA THAT I SHALL SPARE YOU THAT UNPLEASANT TASK WHEN POOR SILVIA DIES
results.transcription: You will forgive me, dear reader. If I have made you attend the funeral of Sylvia ten years before her death, believe me, I have no intention of performing a miracle. You may console yourself with the idea that I shall spare you that unpleasant task when poor Sylvia dies.

results.reference_text: I NEVER HAD ANY FAMILY
results.transcription: I never had any family.

results.reference_text: I HAD A NAME I BELIEVE IN MY YOUNG DAYS BUT I HAVE FORGOTTEN IT SINCE I HAVE BEEN IN SERVICE
results.transcription: I had a name I believe in my young days, but I have forgotten it since I have been in service.

results.reference_text: I SHALL CALL YOU ESPRIT
results.transcription: I shall call you as free.

results.reference_text: YOU DO ME A GREAT HONOUR
results.transcription: You do me a great honor.

results.reference_text: HERE GO AND GET ME CHANGE FOR A LOUIS I HAVE IT SIR
results.transcription: Here. Go and get me change for a Louis. I have it, sir.

results.reference_text: AT YOUR SERVICE SIR
results.transcription: At your service, sir.

results.reference_text: MADAME QUINSON BESIDES CAN ANSWER YOUR ENQUIRIES
results.transcription: Madame Quentin, besides, can answer your inquiries.

results.reference_text: I SEE A QUANTITY OF CHAIRS FOR HIRE AT THE RATE OF ONE SOU MEN READING THE NEWSPAPER UNDER THE SHADE OF THE TREES GIRLS AND MEN BREAKFASTING EITHER ALONE OR IN COMPANY WAITERS WHO WERE RAPIDLY GOING UP AND DOWN A NARROW STAIRCASE HIDDEN UNDER THE FOLIAGE
results.transcription: I see a quantity of chairs for hire at the rate of one sue. Men reading the newspaper under the shade of the trees, girls and men breakfasting either alone or in company, waiters who were rapidly going up and down a narrow staircase hidden under the foliage.

results.reference_text: I SIT DOWN AT A SMALL TABLE A WAITER COMES IMMEDIATELY TO ENQUIRE MY WISHES
results.transcription: I sit down at a small table. A waiter comes immediately to inquire my wishes.

results.reference_text: I TELL HIM TO GIVE ME SOME COFFEE IF IT IS GOOD
results.transcription: I tell him to give me some coffee if it is good.

results.reference_text: THEN TURNING TOWARDS ME HE SAYS THAT I LOOK LIKE A FOREIGNER AND WHEN I SAY THAT I AM AN ITALIAN HE BEGINS TO SPEAK TO ME OF THE COURT OF THE CITY OF THE THEATRES AND AT LAST HE OFFERS TO ACCOMPANY ME EVERYWHERE
results.transcription: Then, turning towards me, he says that I look like a foreigner, and when I say that I am an Italian, he begins to speak to me of the court, the city, of the theaters, and at last he offers to accompany me everywhere.

results.reference_text: I THANK HIM AND TAKE MY LEAVE
results.transcription: I thank him and take my leave.

results.reference_text: I ADDRESS HIM IN ITALIAN AND HE ANSWERS VERY WITTILY BUT HIS WAY OF SPEAKING MAKES ME SMILE AND I TELL HIM WHY
results.transcription: I address him in Italian, and he answers very bitterly, but his way of speaking makes me smile, and I tell him why.

results.reference_text: MY REMARK PLEASES HIM BUT I SOON PROVE TO HIM THAT IT IS NOT THE RIGHT WAY TO SPEAK HOWEVER PERFECT MAY HAVE BEEN THE LANGUAGE OF THAT ANCIENT WRITER
results.transcription: My remark pleases him, but I soon prove to him that it is not the right way to speak. However, perfects may have been the language of that ancient writer.

results.reference_text: I SEE A CROWD IN ONE CORNER OF THE GARDEN EVERYBODY STANDING STILL AND LOOKING UP
results.transcription: I see a crowd in one corner of the garden. Everybody standing still on looking up.

results.reference_text: IS THERE NOT A MERIDIAN EVERYWHERE
results.transcription: Is there not a meridian everywhere?

results.reference_text: YES BUT THE MERIDIAN OF THE PALAIS ROYAL IS THE MOST EXACT
results.transcription: Yes, but the meridian of the Palais Royale is the most exact.

results.reference_text: THAT IS TRUE BADAUDERIE
results.transcription: That is true bad dealt grey.

results.reference_text: ALL THESE HONEST PERSONS ARE WAITING THEIR TURN TO GET THEIR SNUFF BOXES FILLED
results.transcription: All these honest persons are waiting their turn to get their snuff boxes filled.

results.reference_text: IT IS SOLD EVERYWHERE BUT FOR THE LAST THREE WEEKS NOBODY WILL USE ANY SNUFF BUT THAT SOLD AT THE CIVET CAT
results.transcription: It is sold everywhere, but for the last three weeks nobody will use any snuff, but that sold at the Sivet Cat.

results.reference_text: IS IT BETTER THAN ANYWHERE ELSE
results.transcription: Is it better than anywhere else?

results.reference_text: BUT HOW DID SHE MANAGE TO RENDER IT SO FASHIONABLE
results.transcription: But how did she manage to render it so fashionable?

results.reference_text: SIMPLY BY STOPPING HER CARRIAGE TWO OR THREE TIMES BEFORE THE SHOP TO HAVE HER SNUFF BOX FILLED AND BY SAYING ALOUD TO THE YOUNG GIRL WHO HANDED BACK THE BOX THAT HER SNUFF WAS THE VERY BEST IN PARIS
results.transcription: Simply by stopping her carriage two or three times before the shop to have her snuff box filled. And by saying aloud to the young girl who handed back the box that her snuff was the very best in Paris.

results.reference_text: YOU ARE NOW IN THE ONLY COUNTRY IN THE WORLD WHERE WIT CAN MAKE A FORTUNE BY SELLING EITHER A GENUINE OR A FALSE ARTICLE IN THE FIRST CASE IT RECEIVES THE WELCOME OF INTELLIGENT AND TALENTED PEOPLE AND IN THE SECOND FOOLS ARE ALWAYS READY TO REWARD IT FOR SILLINESS IS TRULY A CHARACTERISTIC OF THE PEOPLE HERE AND HOWEVER WONDERFUL IT MAY APPEAR SILLINESS IS THE DAUGHTER OF WIT
results.transcription: You are now in the only country in the world where wit can make a fortune by selling either a genuine or a false article. In the first case, it receives the welcome of intelligent and talented people. And in the second, fools are always ready to reward it. For silliness is truly a characteristic of the people here. And however wonderful it may appear, silliness is the daughter of wit.

results.reference_text: LET A MAN RUN AND EVERYBODY WILL RUN AFTER HIM THE CROWD WILL NOT STOP UNLESS THE MAN IS PROVED TO BE MAD BUT TO PROVE IT IS INDEED A DIFFICULT TASK BECAUSE WE HAVE A CROWD OF MEN WHO MAD FROM THEIR BIRTH ARE STILL CONSIDERED WISE
results.transcription: Let a man run and everybody will run after him. The crowd will not stop unless the man is proved to be mad. But to prove it is indeed a difficult task because we have a crowd of men who, mad from their birth, are still considered wise.

results.reference_text: IT SEEMS TO ME I REPLIED THAT SUCH APPROVAL SUCH RATIFICATION OF THE OPINION EXPRESSED BY THE KING THE PRINCES OF THE BLOOD ET CETERA IS RATHER A PROOF OF THE AFFECTION FELT FOR THEM BY THE NATION FOR THE FRENCH CARRY THAT AFFECTION TO SUCH AN EXTENT THAT THEY BELIEVE THEM INFALLIBLE
results.transcription: It seems to me, I replied, that such approval, such ratification of the opinion expressed by the king, the princes of the blood, etc., is rather a proof of the affection felt for them by the nation, for the French carry that affection to such an extent that they believe them infallible.

results.reference_text: WHEN THE KING COMES TO PARIS EVERYBODY CALLS OUT VIVE LE ROI
results.transcription: When the king comes to Paris, everybody calls out Vivaloroy.

results.reference_text: SHE INTRODUCED ME TO ALL HER GUESTS AND GAVE ME SOME PARTICULARS RESPECTING EVERY ONE OF THEM
results.transcription: She introduced me to all her guests and gave me some particulars respecting every one of them.

results.reference_text: WHAT SIR I SAID TO HIM AM I FORTUNATE ENOUGH TO SEE YOU
results.transcription: What, sir, I said to him, am I fortunate enough to see you?

results.reference_text: HE HIMSELF RECITED THE SAME PASSAGE IN FRENCH AND POLITELY POINTED OUT THE PARTS IN WHICH HE THOUGHT THAT I HAD IMPROVED ON THE ORIGINAL
results.transcription: He himself recited the same passage in French, and politely pointed out the parts in which he thought that I had improved on the original.

results.reference_text: FOR THE FIRST DAY SIR I THINK THAT WHAT YOU HAVE DONE GIVES GREAT HOPES OF YOU AND WITHOUT ANY DOUBT YOU WILL MAKE RAPID PROGRESS
results.transcription: For the first day, sir, I think that what you have done gives great hopes of you, and without any doubt you will make rapid progress.

results.reference_text: I BELIEVE IT SIR AND THAT IS WHAT I FEAR THEREFORE THE PRINCIPAL OBJECT OF MY VISIT HERE IS TO DEVOTE MYSELF ENTIRELY TO THE STUDY OF THE FRENCH LANGUAGE
results.transcription: I believe it, sir, and that is what I fear. Therefore, the principal object of my visit here is to devote myself entirely to the study of the French language.

results.reference_text: I AM A VERY UNPLEASANT PUPIL ALWAYS ASKING QUESTIONS CURIOUS TROUBLESOME INSATIABLE AND EVEN SUPPOSING THAT I COULD MEET WITH THE TEACHER I REQUIRE I AM AFRAID I AM NOT RICH ENOUGH TO PAY HIM
results.transcription: I am a very unpleasant pupil, always asking questions, curious, troublesome, insatiable, and even supposing that I could meet with the teacher I require. I am afraid I am not rich enough to pay him.

results.reference_text: I RESIDE IN THE MARAIS RUE DE DOUZE PORTES
results.transcription: I reside in the Marais Groude du Sport.

results.reference_text: I WILL MAKE YOU TRANSLATE THEM INTO FRENCH AND YOU NEED NOT BE AFRAID OF MY FINDING YOU INSATIABLE
results.transcription: I will make you translate them into French and you need not be afraid of my finding you insatiable.

results.reference_text: HE HAD A GOOD APPETITE COULD TELL A GOOD STORY WITHOUT LAUGHING WAS CELEBRATED FOR HIS WITTY REPARTEES AND HIS SOCIABLE MANNERS BUT HE SPENT HIS LIFE AT HOME SELDOM GOING OUT AND SEEING HARDLY ANYONE BECAUSE HE ALWAYS HAD A PIPE IN HIS MOUTH AND WAS SURROUNDED BY AT LEAST TWENTY CATS WITH WHICH HE WOULD AMUSE HIMSELF ALL DAY
results.transcription: He had a good appetite, could tell a good story without laughing, was celebrated for his woody repartees and his sociable manners, but he spent his life at home, seldom going out and seeing hardly anyone, because he always had a pipe in his mouth and was surrounded by at least 20 cats with which he would amuse himself all day.

results.reference_text: HIS HOUSEKEEPER HAD THE MANAGEMENT OF EVERYTHING SHE NEVER ALLOWED HIM TO BE IN NEED OF ANYTHING AND SHE GAVE NO ACCOUNT OF HIS MONEY WHICH SHE KEPT ALTOGETHER BECAUSE HE NEVER ASKED HER TO RENDER ANY ACCOUNTS
results.transcription: His housekeeper had the management of everything. She never allowed him to be in need of anything, and she gave no account of his money, which she kept altogether, because he never asked her to render any accounts.

results.reference_text: ON THE SIXTH OF APRIL EIGHTEEN THIRTY THE CHURCH OF JESUS CHRIST OF LATTER DAY SAINTS WAS FORMALLY ORGANIZED AND THUS TOOK ON A LEGAL EXISTENCE
results.transcription: On 6 April 1830, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints was formerly organized and thus took on a legal existence.

results.reference_text: ITS ORIGIN WAS SMALL A GERM AN INSIGNIFICANT SEED HARDLY TO BE THOUGHT OF AS LIKELY TO AROUSE OPPOSITION
results.transcription: its origin was small, a germ, an insignificant seed, hardly to be thought of as likely to arouse opposition.

results.reference_text: INSTEAD OF BUT SIX REGULARLY AFFILIATED MEMBERS AND AT MOST TWO SCORE OF ADHERENTS THE ORGANIZATION NUMBERS TODAY MANY HUNDRED THOUSAND SOULS
results.transcription: Instead of but six regularly affiliated members, and at most two square of adherents, the organization numbers today many hundred thousand souls.

results.reference_text: IN PLACE OF A SINGLE HAMLET IN THE SMALLEST CORNER OF WHICH THE MEMBERS COULD HAVE CONGREGATED THERE NOW ARE ABOUT SEVENTY STAKES OF ZION AND ABOUT SEVEN HUNDRED ORGANIZED WARDS EACH WARD AND STAKE WITH ITS FULL COMPLEMENT OF OFFICERS AND PRIESTHOOD ORGANIZATIONS
results.transcription: In place of a single hamlet, in the smallest corner of which the members could have congregated, there now are about 70 stakes of Zion and about 700 organized wards, each ward and stake with its full complement of officers and priesthood organizations.

results.reference_text: THE PRACTISE OF GATHERING ITS PROSELYTES INTO ONE PLACE PREVENTS THE BUILDING UP AND STRENGTHENING OF FOREIGN BRANCHES AND INASMUCH AS EXTENSIVE AND STRONG ORGANIZATIONS ARE SELDOM MET WITH ABROAD VERY ERRONEOUS IDEAS EXIST CONCERNING THE STRENGTH OF THE CHURCH
results.transcription: The practice of gathering its proselytes into one place prevents the building up and strengthening of foreign branches. And inasmuch as extensive and strong organizations are seldom met with abroad, very erroneous ideas exist concerning the strength of the Church.

results.reference_text: NEVERTHELESS THE MUSTARD SEED AMONG THE SMALLEST OF ALL SEEDS HAS ATTAINED THE PROPORTIONS OF A TREE AND THE BIRDS OF THE AIR ARE NESTING IN ITS BRANCHES THE ACORN IS NOW AN OAK OFFERING PROTECTION AND THE SWEETS OF SATISFACTION TO EVERY EARNEST PILGRIM JOURNEYING ITS WAY FOR TRUTH
results.transcription: Nevertheless, the mustard seed, among the smallest of all seeds, has attained the proportions of a tree, and the birds of the air are nesting in its branches. The acorn is now in oak, offering protection, and the suites of satisfaction, to every earnest pilgrim journeying its way for truth.

results.reference_text: THEIR EYES WERE FROM THE FIRST TURNED IN ANTICIPATION TOWARD THE EVENING SUN NOT MERELY THAT THE WORK OF PROSELYTING SHOULD BE CARRIED ON IN THE WEST BUT THAT THE HEADQUARTERS OF THE CHURCH SHOULD BE THERE ESTABLISHED
results.transcription: Their eyes were from the first, turned in anticipation toward the evening sun. Not merely that the work of proselyting should be carried on in the west, but that the headquarters of the church should be there established.

results.reference_text: THE BOOK OF MORMON HAD TAUGHT THE PEOPLE THE TRUE ORIGIN AND DESTINY OF THE AMERICAN INDIANS AND TOWARD THIS DARK SKINNED REMNANT OF A ONCE MIGHTY PEOPLE THE MISSIONARIES OF MORMONISM EARLY TURNED THEIR EYES AND WITH THEIR EYES WENT THEIR HEARTS AND THEIR HOPES
results.transcription: The Book of Mormon had taught the people the true origin and destiny of the American Indians, and toward this dark-skinned remnant of a once mighty people. The missionaries of Mormonism early turned their eyes, and with their eyes went their hearts and their hopes.

results.reference_text: IT IS NOTABLE THAT THE INDIAN TRIBES HAVE GENERALLY REGARDED THE RELIGION OF THE LATTER DAY SAINTS WITH FAVOR SEEING IN THE BOOK OF MORMON STRIKING AGREEMENT WITH THEIR OWN TRADITIONS
results.transcription: It is notable that the Indian tribes have generally regarded the religion of the Latter-day Saints with favor, seeing in the Book of Mormon striking agreement with their own traditions.

results.reference_text: THE FIRST WELL ESTABLISHED SEAT OF THE CHURCH WAS IN THE PRETTY LITTLE TOWN OF KIRTLAND OHIO ALMOST WITHIN SIGHT OF LAKE ERIE AND HERE SOON ROSE THE FIRST TEMPLE OF MODERN TIMES
results.transcription: The first well-established seat of the church was in the pretty little town of Kirtland, Ohio, almost within sight of Lake Erie. And here soon rose the first temple of modern times.

results.reference_text: TO THE FERVENT LATTER DAY SAINT A TEMPLE IS NOT SIMPLY A CHURCH BUILDING A HOUSE FOR RELIGIOUS ASSEMBLY
results.transcription: To the Fervent Latter-day Saint, a temple is not simply a church building, a house for religious assembly.

results.reference_text: SOON THOUSANDS OF CONVERTS HAD RENTED OR PURCHASED HOMES IN MISSOURI INDEPENDENCE JACKSON COUNTY BEING THEIR CENTER BUT FROM THE FIRST THEY WERE UNPOPULAR AMONG THE MISSOURIANS
results.transcription: Soon thousands of converts had rented or purchased homes in Missouri, Independence Jackson County being their center. But from the first, they were unpopular among the Missyrians.

results.reference_text: THE LIEUTENANT GOVERNOR LILBURN W BOGGS AFTERWARD GOVERNOR WAS A PRONOUNCED MORMON HATER AND THROUGHOUT THE PERIOD OF THE TROUBLES HE MANIFESTED SYMPATHY WITH THE PERSECUTORS
results.transcription: The lieutenant governor, Littleburn W. Boggs, afterward governor, was a pronounced Mormon hater, and throughout the period of the trebles, he manifests his sympathy with the persecutors.

results.reference_text: THEIR SUFFERINGS HAVE NEVER YET BEEN FITLY CHRONICLED BY HUMAN SCRIBE
results.transcription: Their sufferings have never yet been fiddly chronicle by human scribe.

results.reference_text: MAKING THEIR WAY ACROSS THE RIVER MOST OF THE REFUGEES FOUND SHELTER AMONG THE MORE HOSPITABLE PEOPLE OF CLAY COUNTY AND AFTERWARD ESTABLISHED THEMSELVES IN CALDWELL COUNTY THEREIN FOUNDING THE CITY OF FAR WEST
results.transcription: making their way across the river. Most of the refugees found shelter among the more hospitable people of Clay County and afterward established themselves in Caldwell County. They were in the city of Far West.

results.reference_text: A SMALL SETTLEMENT HAD BEEN FOUNDED BY MORMON FAMILIES ON SHOAL CREEK AND HERE ON THE THIRTIETH OF OCTOBER EIGHTEEN THIRTY EIGHT A COMPANY OF TWO HUNDRED AND FORTY FELL UPON THE HAPLESS SETTLERS AND BUTCHERED A SCORE
results.transcription: A small settlement had been founded by Mormon families on Shoal Creek, and here on the 30th of October, 1838, a company of 240 fell upon the hapless settlers and butcher the score.

results.reference_text: BE IT SAID TO THE HONOR OF SOME OF THE OFFICERS ENTRUSTED WITH THE TERRIBLE COMMISSION THAT WHEN THEY LEARNED ITS TRUE SIGNIFICANCE THEY RESIGNED THEIR AUTHORITY RATHER THAN HAVE ANYTHING TO DO WITH WHAT THEY DESIGNATED A COLD BLOODED BUTCHERY
results.transcription: Be it said to the honor of some of the officers entrusted with a terrible commission, that when they learned its true significance, they resigned their authority rather than have anything to do with what they designated a cold-blooded butchery.

results.reference_text: OH WHAT A RECORD TO READ WHAT A PICTURE TO GAZE UPON HOW AWFUL THE FACT
results.transcription: Oh, what a record to read. What a picture to gaze upon. How awful the fact.

results.reference_text: AMERICAN SCHOOL BOYS READ WITH EMOTIONS OF HORROR OF THE ALBIGENSES DRIVEN BEATEN AND KILLED WITH A PAPAL LEGATE DIRECTING THE BUTCHERY AND OF THE VAUDOIS HUNTED AND HOUNDED LIKE BEASTS AS THE EFFECT OF A ROYAL DECREE AND THEY YET SHALL READ IN THE HISTORY OF THEIR OWN COUNTRY OF SCENES AS TERRIBLE AS THESE IN THE EXHIBITION OF INJUSTICE AND INHUMAN HATE
results.transcription: American schoolboys read with emotions of horror, of the Alba Jensus, driven, beaten, and killed, with a papal legate directing the butchery. And of the Faudoir, hunted and hounded like beasts, as the effect of a royal decree. And they yet shall read in the history of their own country, of scenes as terrible as these, in the exhibition of injustice and inhuman hate.

results.reference_text: WHO BEGAN THE QUARREL WAS IT THE MORMONS
results.transcription: Who began the quarrel? Was it the Mormons?

results.reference_text: AS A SAMPLE OF THE PRESS COMMENTS AGAINST THE BRUTALITY OF THE MISSOURIANS I QUOTE A PARAGRAPH FROM THE QUINCY ARGUS MARCH SIXTEENTH EIGHTEEN THIRTY NINE
results.transcription: As a sample of the press comments against the brutality of the Missyrians, I quote a paragraph from the Quincy Argus, March 16, 1839.

results.reference_text: IT WILL BE OBSERVED THAT AN ORGANIZED MOB AIDED BY MANY OF THE CIVIL AND MILITARY OFFICERS OF MISSOURI WITH GOVERNOR BOGGS AT THEIR HEAD HAVE BEEN THE PROMINENT ACTORS IN THIS BUSINESS INCITED TOO IT APPEARS AGAINST THE MORMONS BY POLITICAL HATRED AND BY THE ADDITIONAL MOTIVES OF PLUNDER AND REVENGE
results.transcription: It will be observed that an organized mob, aided by many of the civil and military officers of Missouri, with Governor Boggs at their head, have been the prominent actors in this business. Insighted, too, it appears against the Mormons by political hatred, and by the additional motives of plunder and revenge.

results.reference_text: THE ARMY FOUND THE PEOPLE IN POVERTY AND LEFT THEM IN COMPARATIVE WEALTH
results.transcription: The army found the people in poverty and left them in comparative wealth.

results.reference_text: BUT A WORD FURTHER CONCERNING THE EXPEDITION IN GENERAL
results.transcription: but a word further concerning the expedition in general.

results.reference_text: IT WAS THROUGH FLOYD'S ADVICE THAT BUCHANAN ORDERED THE MILITARY EXPEDITION TO UTAH OSTENSIBLY TO INSTALL CERTAIN FEDERAL OFFICIALS AND TO REPRESS AN ALLEGED INFANTILE REBELLION WHICH IN FACT HAD NEVER COME INTO EXISTENCE BUT IN REALITY TO FURTHER THE INTERESTS OF THE SECESSIONISTS
results.transcription: It was through Floyd's advice that Buchanan ordered the military expedition to Utah, ostensibly, to install certain federal officials and to repress an alleged infantile rebellion, which in fact had never come into existence, but in reality to further the interests of the secessionists.

results.reference_text: MOREOVER HAD THE PEOPLE BEEN INCLINED TO REBELLION WHAT GREATER OPPORTUNITY COULD THEY HAVE WISHED
results.transcription: Moreover, had the people been inclined to rebellion, what greater opportunity could they have wished?

results.reference_text: ALREADY A NORTH AND A SOUTH WERE TALKED OF WHY NOT SET UP ALSO A WEST
results.transcription: Already in North and South we're talkative. Why not set up also a West?

results.reference_text: THEY KNEW NO NORTH NO SOUTH NO EAST NO WEST THEY STOOD POSITIVELY BY THE CONSTITUTION AND WOULD HAVE NOTHING TO DO IN THE BLOODY STRIFE BETWEEN BROTHERS UNLESS INDEED THEY WERE SUMMONED BY THE AUTHORITY TO WHICH THEY HAD ALREADY ONCE LOYALLY RESPONDED TO FURNISH MEN AND ARMS FOR THEIR COUNTRY'S NEED
results.transcription: They knew no North, no South, no East, no West. They stood positively by the Constitution, and would have nothing to do in the bloody strife between brothers. Unless indeed they were summoned by the authority to which they had already once lawfully responded, to furnish men and arms for the country's need.

results.reference_text: WHAT THE LATTER DAY SAINTS CALL CELESTIAL MARRIAGE IS CHARACTERISTIC OF THE CHURCH AND IS IN VERY GENERAL PRACTISE BUT OF CELESTIAL MARRIAGE PLURALITY OF WIVES WAS AN INCIDENT NEVER AN ESSENTIAL
results.transcription: What the Latter-day Saints call celestial marriage is characteristic of the Church, and is in very general practice. But of celestial marriage, plurality of wives was an incident, never an essential.

results.reference_text: WE BELIEVE IN A LITERAL RESURRECTION AND AN ACTUAL HEREAFTER IN WHICH FUTURE STATE SHALL BE RECOGNIZED EVERY SANCTIFIED AND AUTHORIZED RELATIONSHIP EXISTING HERE ON EARTH OF PARENT AND CHILD BROTHER AND SISTER HUSBAND AND WIFE
results.transcription: We believe in a literal resurrection and an actual hereafter, in which future states shall be recognized every sanctified and authorized relationship existing here on Earth. Of parent and child, brother and sister, husband and wife.

results.reference_text: IT HAS BEEN MY PRIVILEGE TO TREAD THE SOIL OF MANY LANDS TO OBSERVE THE CUSTOMS AND STUDY THE HABITS OF MORE NATIONS THAN ONE AND I HAVE YET TO FIND THE PLACE AND MEET THE PEOPLE WHERE AND WITH WHOM THE PURITY OF MAN AND WOMAN IS HELD MORE PRECIOUS THAN AMONG THE MALIGNED MORMONS IN THE MOUNTAIN VALLEYS OF THE WEST
results.transcription: It has been my privilege to tread the soil of many lands, to observe the customs and study the habits of more nations than one. And I have yet to find the place and meet the people, where and with whom the purity of man and woman is held more precious than among the maligned Mormons and the mountain valleys of the West.

results.reference_text: AT THE INCEPTION OF PLURAL MARRIAGE AMONG THE LATTER DAY SAINTS THERE WAS NO LAW NATIONAL OR STATE AGAINST ITS PRACTISE
results.transcription: At the inception of plural marriage among the Latter-day Saints, there was no law, national or state against its practice.

results.reference_text: IN EIGHTEEN SIXTY TWO A LAW WAS ENACTED WITH THE PURPOSE OF SUPPRESSING PLURAL MARRIAGE AND AS HAD BEEN PREDICTED IN THE NATIONAL SENATE PRIOR TO ITS PASSAGE IT LAY FOR MANY YEARS A DEAD LETTER
results.transcription: In 1862, a law was enacted with the purpose of suppressing plural marriage, and as had been predicted in the National Senate prior to its passage, it lay for many years a dead letter.

results.transcription: After an apprenticeship on a merchant ship he had entered the Imperial Navy, and had already reached the rank of lieutenant when the Count appointed him to the charge of his own private yacht, in which he was accustomed to spend by far the greater part of his time, throughout the winter generally cruising in the Mediterranean, whilst in the summer he visited more northern waters.

results.reference_text: THE LATE ASTOUNDING EVENTS HOWEVER HAD RENDERED PROCOPE MANIFESTLY UNEASY AND NOT THE LESS SO FROM HIS CONSCIOUSNESS THAT THE COUNT SECRETLY PARTOOK OF HIS OWN ANXIETY
results.transcription: The late astounding events, however, had rendered pro-cope manifestly uneasy, and not the less so from his consciousness that the Count secretly partook of his own anxiety.

results.reference_text: STEAM UP AND CANVAS SPREAD THE SCHOONER STARTED EASTWARDS
results.transcription: Steam up and canvas spread the schooner started eastwards.

results.reference_text: ALTHOUGH ONLY A MODERATE BREEZE WAS BLOWING THE SEA WAS ROUGH A CIRCUMSTANCE TO BE ACCOUNTED FOR ONLY BY THE DIMINUTION IN THE FORCE OF THE EARTH'S ATTRACTION RENDERING THE LIQUID PARTICLES SO BUOYANT THAT BY THE MERE EFFECT OF OSCILLATION THEY WERE CARRIED TO A HEIGHT THAT WAS QUITE UNPRECEDENTED
results.transcription: Although only a moderate breeze was blowing, the sea was rough. A circumstance to be accounted for only by the diminution in the force of the earth's attraction, rendering the liquid particles so buoyant, that by the mere effect of oscillation they were carried to a height that was quite unprecedented.

results.reference_text: FOR A FEW MILES SHE FOLLOWED THE LINE HITHERTO PRESUMABLY OCCUPIED BY THE COAST OF ALGERIA BUT NO LAND APPEARED TO THE SOUTH
results.transcription: For a few miles, she followed the line hitherto presumably occupied by the coast of Algeria, but no land appeared to the south.

results.reference_text: THE LOG AND THE COMPASS THEREFORE WERE ABLE TO BE CALLED UPON TO DO THE WORK OF THE SEXTANT WHICH HAD BECOME UTTERLY USELESS
results.transcription: The log and the compass, therefore, were able to be called upon to do the work of the sextant, which had become utterly useless.

results.transcription: The earth has undoubtedly entered upon a new orbit, but she is not incurring any probable risk of being precipitated onto the sun.

results.transcription: And what demonstration do you offer, asked Servadak eagerly, that it will not happen?

results.transcription: All the images of his past life floated upon his memory. His thoughts sped away to his native France, only to return again to wonder whether the depths of ocean would reveal any traces of the Algerian metropolis.

results.transcription: Is it not impossible, he murmured aloud, that any city should disappear so completely?

results.transcription: Another circumstance was most remarkable.

results.transcription: To the surprise of all, and especially of Lieutenant Prokope, the line indicated a bottom at a nearly uniform depth of from four to five fathoms. And although the sounding was persevered with continuously for more than two hours over a considerable area, the differences of level were insignificant, not corresponding in any degree to what would be expected over the sight of a city that had been terraced like the seats of an amphitheater.

results.reference_text: YOU MUST SEE LIEUTENANT I SHOULD THINK THAT WE ARE NOT SO NEAR THE COAST OF ALGERIA AS YOU IMAGINED
results.transcription: You must see, Lieutenant, I should think that we are not so near the coast of Algeria as you imagined.

results.transcription: After pondering a while, he said, if we were farther away, I should expect to find a depth of two or three hundred fathoms instead of five fathoms. Five fathoms!
